markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **verified Bernoulli terminal allocation**, after resolving the disagreement between recorded 64/64 branch counts and definitions claiming Bernoulli(0.75). Existing diagnostics cannot establish that the proposed intervention ran.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. First, separately normalized branches retain coefficients 0.5/0.5 despite allocating 75% of examples to terminal supervision. Allocation therefore changes sampling precision and target volume without automatically increasing terminal objective weight. Second, snapshots and metric definitions describe different samplers. Checkpoint-bound measured provenance is necessary before attributing outcomes to either sampler. Third, sampled negative-win rates are below 7%, while user RankMe is lower than item RankMe. Neither observation establishes ranking improvement, representation collapse, or the cause of users’ relevance complaints.

Three literature insights sharpen the experiment. BERT4Rec already uses final-item masking to address appended-MASK inference [1]. Its contribution supports this intervention but limits its originality. PCGrad and GradNorm distinguish gradient conflict from gradient magnitude [2,3]. Neither supports inferring gradient influence from example shares. Sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking [4]. The pinned validation objective and twenty-user recommendation audit must therefore remain separate.

The resulting framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Controlled variable | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision allocation | Bernoulli branch assignment | Realized examples, targets, denominators |
| Optimization mechanism | Branch gradient variability | Repeated coefficient-weighted gradients |
| Context relevance | Recent-history dependence | Paired frozen-context perturbations |

Three atomic ideas follow; scores are originality/potential/difficulty, where higher difficulty means more implementation effort.

- **Verified Bernoulli allocation — 3/6/4.** Originality: stronger experimental identification; established sampling technique. Potential: enables interpretable follow-ups; ranking benefit remains unproven. Difficulty: local sampler change; checkpoint accounting requires care [1].
- **Branch-gradient variance audit — 4/6/6.** Originality: connects allocation to measured optimization noise; standard gradient statistics. Potential: could motivate later allocation choices; Adam and random denominators complicate interpretation. Difficulty: no architecture change; repeated gradients consume budget [2,3].
- **Recent-context perturbation audit — 3/6/5.** Originality: directly investigates reported stale-interest failures; perturbation methods are established. Potential: identifies sensitivity gaps; cannot establish compatibility or unmet needs. Difficulty: frozen inference is simple; matched controls and user-level uncertainty require care.

At 40% progress, select the first idea. Draw 128 independent Bernoulli(0.75) assignments per update, retain branch-specific context generators, and optimize unchanged separately normalized losses. This explicitly replaces fixed 64/64 allocation; it is not a shared-context corruption experiment. Bind measured accounting and protocol identity to the selected checkpoint, and mark conflicting legacy records as unresolved. Train one BERT4Rec per category; preserve seeds, evaluator, schedule, predictor consistency, and diagnostic interfaces. Accept effectiveness claims only from the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Test independent Bernoulli(0.75) allocation over 128 generated training views in each update, preserving the corrected BERT4Rec branch-specific context generators and 0.5/0.5 separately normalized losses. Bind actual sampler configuration and measured objective accounting to each selected category checkpoint.
idea.motivation: The supplied snapshots report fixed 64/64 allocation, whereas their definitions describe Bernoulli allocation. Resolving that contradiction is essential to interpreting the proposed intervention. Terminal masking matches appended-MASK inference, but allocating more terminal examples does not itself increase its separately normalized loss coefficient or guarantee improved HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Apply this intervention to the host-supplied corrected baseline; its executable source is absent from the prompt, so the pseudocode is an integration contract rather than a standalone train.py. Explicitly record conversion from fixed 64/64 generated-view allocation to 128 independent Bernoulli assignments. Preserve branch-conditional user sampling, cutoff distribution, truncation, positional convention, 0.15 MASK-only reconstruction and fallback, full-real-item tied output head, optimizer, validation cadence, patience, and earliest-maximum checkpoint rule. Preserve each nonempty branch's 0.5 coefficient and target-count denominator; absent branches contribute zero without redistribution. With B=128, terminal absence probability is 0.25^128 and reconstruction absence probability is 0.75^128. Variable target-count normalization means this is not an exact population-gradient invariance claim. Save actual per-update branch examples, target counts, detached CE sums, denominators, coefficient masses, objective contributions, and empty counts; distinguish aggregate CE ratios from mean batch objectives. Bind summaries to checkpoint identity, selected epoch, cumulative interval, and sampler version. Generate metric definitions from saved configuration; report incompatible legacy metadata as unresolved rather than rewriting measured counts. Preserve all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and charge all execution to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Use one independently trained model/checkpoint per category without fusion or averaging. Preserve sample_batch, ModelView.model as the actual module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and history/metadata handles. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); diagnostic batches remain B x L tensors. Inference truncates history to L-1, appends reserved MASK, left-pads, and reads the maximum nonpadding index. Keep the embedded predictor writer consistent with the checkpoint and compare reloaded predictor scores on identical inputs. Use only supplied histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions; unavailable attributes and simulator traits remain unknown. Keep host evaluation and splits unchanged; use no hidden tests, external data, pretrained weights, or other-trial checkpoints.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    model, optimizer, baseline = host_corrected_bert4rec(category, seed=42)
    protocol = record_actual_configuration(
        allocation_unit='generated_view', total_views=128,
        p_terminal=0.75, coefficients=(0.5, 0.5),
        conversion='fixed 64/64 to independent Bernoulli')
    for epoch in baseline.schedule(max_epochs=200):
        for step in range(200):
            # Use a recorded seeded allocation stream; preserve context generators.
            terminal = allocation_rng.random(128) < 0.75
            batch, provenance = baseline.construct_branch_views(terminal)
            features = model.log2feats(batch.sequence)
            loss = features.sum() * 0.0
            for branch in ('reconstruction', 'terminal'):
                selected = provenance.valid_target_positions(branch)
                count = selected.count()
                if count:
                    ce_sum = baseline.real_item_ce_sum(features, batch.labels, selected)
                    contribution = 0.5 * ce_sum / count
                    loss = loss + contribution
                    record_measured(branch, count, ce_sum.detach(), contribution.detach())
                else:
                    record_empty_branch(branch)  # no redistribution
            baseline.optimizer_step(loss)
            record_realized_examples_and_coefficients(provenance)
        baseline.validate_and_select_with_unchanged_rule()
        bind_accounting_to_checkpoint_if_selected(protocol, epoch)
    save_one_selected_category_checkpoint()
    write_matching_embedded_predictor()
    verify_reloaded_predictor_scores_on_identical_inputs()

predict(history, candidates):
    sequence = left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK], length=L)
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    index = maximum_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    return model.predict_score(features[index], candidates)

# Host independently evaluates unchanged macro validation HR@10.
# Diagnostic definitions describe measured checkpoint configuration.
# Legacy allocation contradictions remain explicitly unresolved.

originality.positive: Checkpoint-bound accounting makes the allocation intervention identifiable despite contradictory prior documentation.
originality.negative: Terminal masking, Bernoulli allocation and branch-normalized losses are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Reliable provenance supports later controlled studies of allocation variance and context relevance within one BERT4Rec model.
future_potential.negative: The prescribed probability lacks measured optimality evidence and does not directly resolve compatibility or redundancy complaints.

code_difficulty.positive: The backbone and inference architecture remain unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful branch construction, exact accounting, checkpoint binding and predictor verification require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses final-item masking to address appended-MASK prediction.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal terminal allocation probability for this benchmark.
Its objective formulation does not establish the host implementation's reduction semantics.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
limitations: Gradient conflict is distinct from gradient variance and example allocation.
Does not establish ranking benefits for the proposed BERT4Rec intervention.

related_work.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
contributions: Adapts loss weights using gradient magnitudes and relative training rates.
limitations: Changing objective weights would be a separate intervention.
Example shares alone do not provide its required gradient measurements.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
limitations: Does not justify modifying the pinned host evaluator.
Does not determine which allocation improves this task's fixed candidate-set HR@10.
